name: config_resource_create

name.note: required for a named resourceType, empty for a singleton

collection.note: the core collection: an omitted or empty value means core, and the Tool sends collection=core on every Gateway read and write it makes; any other value fails with invalid_argument before anything is dispatched (D30 owner ruling 5)

preconditionToken.policy: D30 §2: create takes no Precondition token. The D11 collision policy decides instead: the Target must be absent, which is checked against the Gateway before dispatch, and the Gateway's own refusal of an existing name is `conflict`.

targetId.collection: the core collection only: the reads name it as the collection query parameter and the change item carries it as the field its documented POST request-body item schema declares; a type whose item schema does not declare that field, or does not accept core, cannot address a Target here at all and is refused with unsupported_capability before anything is dispatched; a caller-supplied collection is accepted only when it is core, and any other value fails with invalid_argument before anything is dispatched (D30 owner ruling 5)
targetId.denialCodeSource: D30 §7, Tool-scoped; the Phase 3 machinery keeps operation_disabled

requestSchemaValidation.schema: the resource type's documented POST request-body item schema, bundled into a self-contained JSON Schema (internal $refs hoisted to $defs) at capability refresh time
requestSchemaValidation.appliesTo: the complete change item, before dispatch
requestSchemaValidation.unavailableDisposition: a documented create route without a usable request schema, or whose item schema cannot name the core collection, exposes no create route, so the Tool refuses the resource type with unsupported_capability

changeItem: name is included when the documented item schema declares it (its non-singleton create item requires it); the item always names the core collection (D30 owner ruling 5), so a type whose item schema cannot carry that field has no create here; no signature is ever sent, because a create has no Precondition token
collisionPolicy: D11: an existing Target is a `conflict`. It is checked against the Gateway before dispatch, so a collision never consumes the caller's read, and a Target that appears in the race window is refused by the Gateway itself.

rejectionPolicy.rule: D30 §2: an explicit Gateway rejection is the result of the attempt — a 4xx (including 409 for an existing name, which D30 §7 maps to `conflict`) or a 2xx carrying success=false with a problem. No read-back may turn it into a success: a resource showing the requested values may have been created by another writer.
verificationMaySucceedWhen: the Gateway claimed success (2xx with no refusal)
rejectionPolicy.ambiguousAttribution: a competing writer cannot be ruled out for an ambiguous dispatch, so a read-back that shows the Target existing is outcome_unknown, never a success; the Target still absent is not_applied

verification: bounded re-read of the Target, reported as Observed state: the claimed success is confirmed only when the Target exists with the requested values
